questions.question: X can complete half of the work in 20 days and Y can do one-fifth of the same work in 10 days. X started the work and left after 8 days. Then Y took over to complete the remaining work. The total number of days taken by them to complete the work is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

X can complete half of the work in 20 days and Y can do one-fifth of the same work in 10 days. 

X started the work and left after 8 days.

**Concept used:**

Work = Efficiency × time

**Calculation:**

X can complete half of the work in 20 days 

⇒ X can complete the work in 20 × 2 days = 40 days</span

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 660. A shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% and still gets a profit of 10%. If he sells it for Rs. 470, his profit or loss per cent, correct to two decimal places will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The marked price of an article is Rs. 660. 

A shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% and still gets a profit of 10%.

**Formula used:**

CP : MP = (100 - discount%) : (100 + profit%)

loss% = [CP - SP]/CP × 100 

**Calculation:**

CP : MP = 80 : 110

⇒ CP/660 = 8/11

⇒ CP = Rs. 480

∴ If he sells it for Rs. 470 ⇒ SP = Rs. 470

⇒ loss% = [480 - 470]/480 × 100

= (100/48)%

= 2.08%

questions.question: When a number is divided by 3, the remainder is 2. Again, when the quotient is divided by 7, the remainder is 5. What will be the remainder when the original number is divided by 21?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Number = Quotient × Divisor + Remainder

# In such questions, we start from last

**Calculation:**

Let last quotient be 'x'

⇒ Last number = 7x + 5

∴ First number = 3 × (7x + 5) + 2 = 21x + 17

Now, when 21x + 17 is divided by 21 

⇒ Remainder = 17

questions.question: If 3 sin² A + 4 cos² A - 3 = 0, then the value of cot A (where 0 ≤ A ≤ 90°) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

3 sin2 A + 4 cos2 A - 3 = 0

**Formula used: **

sin2 A + cos2 A = 1

**Calculation:**

3 sin2 A + 4 cos2 A - 3 = 0 ⇒ 3 sin2 A + 3 cos2 A + cos2 A - 3 = 0

⇒ 3 ( sin2 A + cos2 A) + cos2 A - 3 = 0

⇒ 3 + cos2 A - 3 = 0

⇒ cos2 A = 0

⇒ cos A = 0

⇒ A = 90° [∵ 0 ≤ A ≤ 90°]

⇒ cot A = cot 90° = 0

questions.question: If a² + b² + c² + 48 = 8(a + b + c), then what is the value of sqrt[3]{a³-b³+c³} ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a2 + b2 + c2 + 48 = 8(a + b + c)

**Calculation:**

a2 + b2 + c2 + 48 = 8(a + b + c) 

⇒ a2 - 8a + 16 + b2 - 8b + 16 + c2 - 8c + 16 = 0

⇒ (a - 4)² + (b - 4)2 + (c - 4)2 = 0

Now, sum of squares = 0 

⇒ each term is = 0

∴ a - 4 = 0 , b - 4 = 0 and c - 4 = 0

⇒ a = b = c = 4

∴ sqrt[3]{a³-b³+c³} = sqrt[3]{4³-4³+4³} 

= sqrt[3]{4³} 

= 4

questions.question: If x⁴ + x⁻⁴ = 47, x > 0, then the value of (2x - 3)² is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x4 + x-4 = 47, x > 0

**Formula used:**

If x ²ⁿ + x-2n = k then xn + x-n = √(k + 2) and xn - x-n = √(k - 2)

**Calculation:**

⇒ x² + x-2 = √(47 + 2) = √49 = 7

⇒ x + x⁻¹ = √(7 + 2) = √9 = 3 ----(A) and x - x-1 = √(7 - 2) = √5 ----(B)

Adding (A) and (B), we get, x + x = 3 + √5

⇒ 2x - 3 = √5 

∴ (2x - 3)² = 5

questions.question: If Δ ABC ∼ Δ QPR, (ar(Delta ABC))/(ar(Delta PQR))=(4)/(9), AC = 12 cm, AB = 18 cm and BC = 10 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Given: ΔABC ~ ΔQPR and Area(ΔABC)/Area(ΔPQR) = 4/9.

Ratio of corresponding sides = √(4/9) = 2/3.

From similarity ΔABC ~ ΔQPR, side **BC** corresponds to side **PR**.

∴ BC/PR = 2/3 ⇒ 10/PR = 2/3 ⇒ PR = (10 × 3)/2 = 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC ~ ΔQPR

Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔQPR) = 4/9

AB = 18 cm, BC = 10 cm, AC = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides:

Area(Δ1) / Area(Δ2) = (Side₁ / Side₂)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/855d7c0ee70d27a1170e359a8ffb3f4348702568ab5b4c6066018d3ad33ce671.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since ΔABC ~ ΔQPR, the corresponding sides are (AB, QP), (BC, PR), and (AC, QR).

⇒ Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔQPR) = (BC / PR)²

⇒ 4 / 9 = (10 / PR)²

Taking square root on both sides:

⇒ √(4 / 9) = 10 / PR

⇒ 2 / 3 = 10 / PR

⇒ 2 × PR = 10 × 3

⇒ 2 × PR = 30

⇒ PR = 30 / 2

⇒ PR = 15 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area Theorem for Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors.

Perimeter of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P1/P2 = s1/s2.

Similarity Criteria

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy the **AAA** (Angle-Angle-Angle), **SSS** (Side-Side-Side ratio), or **SAS** (Side-Angle-Side ratio) criteria.</p

questions.question: A bus covered 360 km in 6 hours. If it travels at one-fourth of its usual speed, then how much more time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A bus covered 360 km in 6 hours

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/time

**Calculation:**

Usual speed of bus = 360/6 = 60 kmph

If it travels at one-fourth of its usual speed, its speed becomes 1/4 × 60 = 15 kmph

Time taken to cover 360 km with decreased speed = 360/15 = 24 hours

∴ Extra time taken to cover the same distance = 24 - 6 = 18 hours

**Given:**

From a point P, which is at a distance of 13 cm from the centre O of a circle, a pair of tangents PQ and PR of length 12 cm are drawn to the circle.

**Concept used:**

Radius of circle is perpendicular to tangent.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db1360eba778c7b24c829f949c8431441f5455941c6c82a9b8e4156424c9e5d5.png] 

In right triangle PQO, OQ² = OP2 - PQ2 = 13² - 12² = 169 - 144 = 25

⇒ OQ = 5 cm

Now, Area of the quadrilateral PQOR = 2 × Area of right triangle PQO 

= 2 × 1/2 × base × height

= 2 × 1/2 × 5 × 12

= 60 cm²

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio of 7 ∶ 4. If each number is increased by 12, then the ratio becomes 3 ∶ 2. The sum of the number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two numbers are in the ratio of 7 ∶ 4

If each number is increased by 12, then the ratio becomes 3 ∶ 2.

**Calculation:**

Let the two numbers be 7x and 4x

ATQ, (7x + 12) : (4x + 12) = 3 : 2

⇒ 14x + 24 = 12x + 36

⇒ 2x = 12

⇒ x = 6

∴ Sum of numbers = 7x + 4x = 11x = 11 × 6 =66

questions.question: When an article is sold for Rs. 438, there is a loss of 27%. To gain 23%, it should be sold for Rs. x . What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When an article is sold for Rs. 438, there is a loss of 27%

**Formula used:**

SP = [(100 - loss%)/100] × CP = [(100 + profit%)/100] × CP

**Calculation:**

SP of article = Rs. 438, loss = 27% ⇒ CP of article = 438 × 100/(100 - 27) = 438 × 100/73 = 600

Now, to gain 23%, it should be sold for Rs. 600 × (100 + 23)/100 = Rs. 738
